items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：行为的状态或结果

definition_zh: 誓言；承诺；抵押物；发誓；抵押
definition_en: a serious promise, or something handed over as security for a debt, and the act of promising or depositing it
core_image: 举起的右手和一张写好的承诺书，说出口就要兑现
scene: 毕业典礼上，全体新生举起右手，跟着领誓人一句一句念出承诺。Each new member had to pledge loyalty to the group in front of everyone.
sceneCN: 这里用的是动词「郑重许诺」（第 3 个义项：发誓、保证）；句意为每位新成员都得当众承诺忠于这个团体。画面里有举起的右手、台下的同伴和安静下来的会场。

collocations.zh: 发誓献身于；保证致力于

derivatives.zh: 由 pledge 加表示承受方的后缀 -ee 构成，法律上指「接受质押的人」
由 pledge 加表示行为方的后缀 -or 构成，法律上指「出质人；抵押人」
由否定前缀 un- 加 pledge 的过去分词构成，义为「未作承诺的；未抵押的」

senses.title: A solemn promise
senses.definition: a serious promise that you will do something, especially one made in public
senses.definitionCN: 郑重许下、通常当众作出的承诺
senses.example: The government broke its pledge to protect the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 政府违背了保护这片森林的承诺。
senses.why: The word first named a thing handed over as a guarantee; a spoken promise borrowed that image because a word can also be held against you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指交出去的担保物；口头承诺借用同一意象，因为一句话同样可以日后被人拿来对着你算账。

senses.title: Something given as security
senses.definition: an object or sum left with someone as security until a debt is paid or a duty is met
senses.definitionCN: 为担保债务或义务而交给对方保管的物件或款项
senses.example: He left his watch as a pledge for the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他把手表留下作为这笔借款的抵押。
senses.why: In medieval law a pledge was the item physically held, so the object and the promise shared one name from the start.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪的法律里，pledge 就是被实际扣在手里的那件东西，所以「物」与「诺」从一开始就共用一个名字。

senses.title: To promise solemnly
senses.definition: to promise seriously and publicly that you will do something or stay loyal
senses.definitionCN: 郑重而公开地保证要做某事或保持忠诚
senses.example: The company pledged to cut its emissions by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司承诺把排放量削减一半。
senses.why: The verb grew out of the noun: to pledge is to hand over your word the way you hand over a security.
senses.whyCN: 动词是从名词长出来的：to pledge 就是把你的话交出去，方式正如交出一件担保物。

senses.title: To give something as security
senses.definition: to hand over an object or property as a guarantee for a loan
senses.definitionCN: 把物件或财产交出，作为借款的担保
senses.example: She pledged her house to raise money for the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 她抵押了房子，为诊所筹钱。
senses.why: Since the noun named the security itself, the verb could name the act of depositing it, which is why finance keeps this concrete sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词指的就是担保物本身，动词自然可以指「把它交出去」这个动作，所以金融语境里这个具体义项一直活着。

intro.en: Pledge entered English through French as a legal word for a surety, and it is generally thought to go back to a Germanic root rather than to Latin.
intro.cn: pledge 作为法律用语经法语进入英语，本义是「担保」；一般认为它源自日耳曼词根，而非拉丁语。

items.en: Old French plege meant a surety, both the promise and the person or object standing behind it.
items.cn: 古法语 plege 意为担保，既指承诺，也指为承诺作保的人或物。

items.en: The word is generally thought to come from a reconstructed Frankish form plegan, meaning to stand surety; the asterisk marks a form not directly recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词来自法兰克语的重构形式 plegan，义为「担保、负责」；带星号表示这是重构而非直接见于文献的形式。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word into law and trade, where a pledge could be a hostage, a deposit or a formal promise.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词用于法律与交易，pledge 可以是人质、押金，也可以是正式承诺。

items.en: The sense widened from property to conduct, so people began to pledge loyalty, support and good behaviour.
items.cn: 词义从财物扩展到行为，于是人们开始 pledge 忠诚、支持与良好表现。

items.en: Modern English keeps the legal deposit sense and the public promise sense side by side, from pawnshops to election campaigns.
items.cn: 现代英语让「抵押」与「公开承诺」两个义项并存，从当铺一直用到竞选。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers guarantee words built on the same French or Germanic stock; the near-meaning group gathers words for promises and security.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一法语或日耳曼语来源上的担保类词；近义组收表示承诺与担保的词。

entries.definition: The Old French form from which the English word descends.
entries.definitionCN: 英语词所由来的古法语形式。

entries.definition: To beg or argue a case in court; it looks close but comes from a different Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；在法庭上申辩。只是拼写相近，词源来自另一个拉丁名词。

entries.definition: The person who receives a pledge as security.
entries.definitionCN: 接受质押物的一方。

entries.definition: The person who gives property as security.
entries.definitionCN: 交出财产作担保的一方。

entries.definition: A statement that you will certainly do something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示一定会做某事的说法。

entries.definition: A very solemn promise, often religious.
entries.definitionCN: 极郑重的誓言，常带宗教色彩。

entries.definition: A firm assurance that something will happen or work.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事会发生或有效的明确保证。

entries.definition: Money or an item left as security.
entries.definitionCN: 作为担保留下的钱或物。

entries.definition: Property promised to a lender if a loan is not repaid.
entries.definitionCN: 借款不能偿还时交给贷方的抵押财产。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the object held against a debt and grew into the spoken promise that carries the same weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初指被扣下抵债的物件，后来长成同样有分量的口头承诺。

normal.en: A pledge was first a thing left with someone, so the physical image of handing something over is still inside the word.
normal.cn: pledge 最早是留在别人手里的东西，所以「把东西交出去」这个具体画面至今仍藏在词里。

normal.en: Make a pledge uses the noun pattern, while pledge to do uses the verb pattern, and both keep the idea of a binding word.
normal.cn: make a pledge 走名词结构，pledge to do 走动词结构，两者都保留了「话一出口就有约束力」的意思。

normal.en: Election pledge shows the word in public politics, where a promise is made to be judged by voters.
normal.cn: election pledge 把这个词放进公共政治，那里的承诺说出口就是为了让选民日后检验。

normal.en: Pledge oneself to adds a reflexive object, stressing that the speaker personally takes on the duty.
normal.cn: pledge oneself to 加了反身宾语，强调说话人本人把这副担子接了下来。

normal.en: The legal pair pledgee and pledgor splits the two sides of the same security arrangement.
normal.cn: 法律上成对的 pledgee 与 pledgor 把同一项担保安排的两端分开了。

abstract.en: A word for a held object turning into a word for a spoken promise shows how much of trust is about having something at stake.
abstract.cn: 一个指「被扣下的物件」的词转成指「说出的话」，说明信任很大程度上取决于有没有东西押在那里。

abstract.en: Every pledge creates a future that other people are allowed to expect.
abstract.cn: 每一次承诺都造出一个别人有权期待的将来。

abstract.en: The same word covers a pawned watch and a campaign promise because both are securities offered against doubt.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指当掉的手表也指竞选承诺，因为两者都是用来对付怀疑的担保。

examples.en: The government broke its pledge to protect the forest.
examples.cn: 政府违背了保护这片森林的承诺。

examples.en: He left his watch as a pledge for the loan.
examples.cn: 他把手表留下作为这笔借款的抵押。

examples.en: The company pledged to cut its emissions by half.
examples.cn: 这家公司承诺把排放量削减一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑莱吉」——把东西扑到对方手里压着，就是「抵押」，说出口的那句话也一并压上，就成了「誓言」。

root: 古法语 plege（担保）进入英语；一般认为可上溯到法兰克语重构形式 plegan（担保、负责），属日耳曼来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a guarantee held by someone else; it splits into the object deposited and the solemn word given, each with its own noun and verb use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「交到别人手里的担保」；它分成押出去的实物与说出口的郑重的话，两者又各有名词与动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised right hand beside a written promise that must be kept.
core.cn: 核心意象：举起的右手旁边放着一份必须兑现的承诺书。

branches.en: a candidate reading a promise aloud
branches.cn: 候选人当众念出一项承诺

branches.en: a watch left on a lender's desk
branches.cn: 留在放贷人桌上的手表

branches.en: a whole class raising their hands together
branches.cn: 全班一起举起右手

branches.en: the key to a house handed to a bank
branches.cn: 把房门钥匙交给银行

branches.en: a written promise signed in front of witnesses
branches.cn: 在见证人面前签下的书面承诺

intro.en: There is no secure Latin family behind this word; its parts come from French and Germanic sources, with English suffixes building the legal pair.
intro.cn: 这个词背后没有可靠的拉丁词族；它的构件来自法语与日耳曼语，再由英语后缀造出法律上一对身份词。

latinIntro.en: A Latin form is sometimes proposed as an intermediate, but it is itself borrowed from Germanic, so no genuine Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 也有人提出过某个拉丁语中间形式，但它本身借自日耳曼语，因此这里不列真正的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: forming the past and past participle
items.meaningCN: 构成过去式与过去分词

items.meaning: the one who receives a pledge

definition_zh: 充足的；丰富的；丰产的；大量的
definition_en: existing in amounts that are enough or more than enough, especially of a supply, a harvest or repeated instances
core_image: 秋收后的谷仓，麻袋一直码到房梁，伸手就还能再拖一袋
scene: 秋收过后的谷仓里，麻袋一直码到房梁，农户随手还能再拖下一袋。A plentiful harvest meant the village would not worry about food that winter.
sceneCN: 这里说的是「丰产的、物产多的」（第 2 个义项）；句意为丰收让全村那个冬天都不用为吃食发愁。画面里有谷仓、码高的麻袋和堆到门口的谷物。

pos.zh: 充足的；丰富的；丰产的；大量的

derivatives.zh: 由 plentiful 加 -ly 构成，义为「充足地；大量地」
由 plentiful 加 -ness 构成，义为「充足；丰富」
由 plenty 的词干加 -eous 构成，文学用语，义为「丰盛的」
借拉丁 plenitudo 而来，与 plentiful 同源，义为「丰足；充满」

senses.title: More than enough for the need
senses.definition: present in an amount large enough to cover what is needed, usually with something to spare
senses.definitionCN: 数量大到足以满足需要，通常还有富余
senses.example: The clinic has a plentiful supply of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所的干净用水供应充足。
senses.why: The adjective is plenty plus -ful, so it describes a supply that is literally full rather than merely adequate.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由名词 plenty 加 -ful 构成，字面就是「满满的」，强调的不是刚好够用，而是有余。

senses.title: Yielding a large amount
senses.definition: producing a large amount of something, said of land, a season, a harvest or a region
senses.definitionCN: 产出很多东西，用来形容土地、季节、收成或地区
senses.example: The valley is famous for its plentiful fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 这道山谷以盛产水果闻名。
senses.why: Land and seasons are judged by what they give, so the same word moves from the size of a supply to the generosity of its source.
senses.whyCN: 土地和季节是按它们给出的东西来评价的，于是这个词从「供给多」滑到「源头慷慨」。

senses.title: Present in large numbers
senses.titleCN: 大量存在的；为数众多的
senses.definition: found in large numbers, as with examples, opportunities or mistakes rather than physical goods
senses.definitionCN: 数量很多地存在，多用于例子、机会、错误等，而非具体货物
senses.example: Plentiful examples make the grammar rule easier to remember.
senses.exampleCN: 大量例子让这条语法规则更容易记住。
senses.why: Once the word means an oversized amount, it can count anything that keeps appearing, not only goods stacked on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦表示「数量超出所需」，凡是一再出现的东西都能用它来数，不再限于货架上的货品。

intro.en: Plentiful is the adjective built on the noun plenty, and both go back through French to a Latin adjective meaning full.
intro.cn: plentiful 是在名词 plenty 上加后缀构成的形容词，二者都经法语上溯到一个意为「满的」的拉丁形容词。

items.en: Plenus meant full, and it is the root behind both plenty and plentiful.
items.cn: plenus 意为「满的」，是 plenty 与 plentiful 共同的根。

items.en: The noun plenitas named fullness or abundance, the state of being full.
items.cn: 名词 plenitas 指「满、充足」，也就是处于装满的状态。

items.en: Old French plente carried that abundance into French and was used of crops, food and wealth.
items.cn: 古法语 plente 把这层「充足」带入法语，常用于庄稼、食物与财富。

items.en: Middle English took plente as a noun for abundance and later formed an adjective from it.
items.cn: 中古英语把 plente 借作表示「充足」的名词，后来又由它造出形容词。

items.en: Modern English settled the spelling plentiful, using -ful to say that something is full of plenty.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 plentiful，用 -ful 表示「充满 plenty」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the nouns and adjectives of the Latin full family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for large amounts.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「满」这一族的名称与形容词；近义组收表示「数量多」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun behind the adjective, meaning a large amount.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的名词，义为「大量；充足」。

entries.definition: An older adjective for abundant, now mostly literary.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的「丰盛」形容词，现多为文学用语。

entries.definition: The state of being full or complete.
entries.definitionCN: 满盈、充足的状态。

entries.definition: Full or complete, as in a meeting with all members present.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的；全体出席的。

entries.definition: Existing in large quantities, often more formally than plentiful.
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在的，比 plentiful 更正式。

entries.definition: Enough and often more than enough for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 足够且常有富余的。

entries.definition: Produced in large amounts, especially of writing or notes.
entries.definitionCN: 大量产生的，多指文字或笔记。

entries.definition: Generous and giving a lot, often of a harvest.
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨而丰盛的，多形容收成。

normalIntro.en: The adjective is simply the noun plenty wearing the suffix -ful, so every image of a full storehouse belongs to it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词就是名词 plenty 披上 -ful 这件外套，所以凡是「满仓」的画面都归它管。

normal.en: Plentiful is plenty plus -ful, so the ending says full of plenty rather than merely enough.
normal.cn: plentiful 就是 plenty 加 -ful，后缀表明的是「充满大量」，而不只是「够用」。

normal.en: The Latin root plenus, meaning full, also hides inside plenary and plenitude, which both stress completeness.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 plenus 意为「满」，也藏在 plenary 与 plenitude 里，两者都强调「完备」。

normal.en: Plentiful goes with supplies and harvests, because it measures a stock rather than a single object.
normal.cn: plentiful 常与 supply、harvest 一类词搭配，因为它衡量的是存量，而不是单个物件。

normal.en: The adverb plentifully keeps the same meaning and simply adds the manner of giving.
normal.cn: 副词 plentifully 意思不变，只是补上「以何种方式给予」。

normal.en: Unlike plenty, the adjective cannot stand alone before a noun without naming what is abundant.
normal.cn: 与名词 plenty 不同，这个形容词放在名词前时，必须说清是什么东西充足。

abstract.en: A word built from full describes not just quantity but the relief of not having to count.
abstract.cn: 一个由「满」构成的词，描述的不只是数量，还有不必再数的安心。

abstract.en: Plentiful land is judged by what it gives away, which is why the same word can praise a valley.
abstract.cn: 丰饶的土地是按它给出的东西来评价的，所以同一个词也能用来夸一道山谷。

abstract.en: When examples are plentiful, abundance stops being about food and becomes about chances to learn.
abstract.cn: 当例子变得 plentiful，充足就不再关乎食物，而关乎学习的机会。

examples.en: The clinic has a plentiful supply of clean water.
examples.cn: 诊所的干净用水供应充足。

examples.en: The valley is famous for its plentiful fruit.
examples.cn: 这道山谷以盛产水果闻名。

examples.en: Plentiful examples make the grammar rule easier to remember.
examples.cn: 大量例子让这条语法规则更容易记住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑棱提否」——粮袋扑棱棱堆到提不动，多到让人直说「否」也不必愁，就是 plentiful。

root: 拉丁语 plenus（满的）→ plenitas（充足）→ 古法语 plente → 英语名词 plenty，再加后缀 -ful 构成 plentiful。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a stock that is more than full; from it come the producing land, and then any set of repeated instances.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装得满满的存量」；由此分出丰产的土地，再扩展到任何一再出现的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sacks stacked to the roof of a barn, with another one still within reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：麻袋一直码到谷仓屋顶，伸手还够得着下一袋。

branches.en: a water tank filled past the mark
branches.cn: 水罐装到刻度线以上

branches.en: orchard trees bending under fruit
branches.cn: 果树被果实压弯

branches.en: margins crowded with worked examples
branches.cn: 页边写满例题

branches.en: a market table that is never empty
branches.cn: 始终不空的集市摊子

branches.en: a season of good weather and good yields
branches.cn: 风调雨顺又高产的一季

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin adjective of fullness plus an English suffix of fullness, which is why the word doubles the idea of being full.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由拉丁语的「满」加上英语表示「充满」的后缀构成，所以它把「满」这层意思叠了两遍。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 大量；许多；富足；足够地
definition_en: a large amount that is enough or more than enough, and informally an adverb meaning fully or very
core_image: 敞开的粮仓门，谷物堆成小山，多到不必去数
scene: 市集快散场时，果摊老板指着还剩大半的木箱，让你随便挑。There is plenty of time, so nobody needs to hurry.
sceneCN: 这里是「大量、许多」的用法（第 1 个义项），出现在 plenty of 这一结构中；句意为时间很充裕，谁都不必赶。画面里有快收摊的果摊、半箱水果和不再着急的顾客。

derivatives.zh: 由 plenty 的词干加 -eous 构成，文学用语，义为「丰盛的；大量的」
借拉丁 plenitudo 而来，与 plenty 同源，义为「丰足；充满」

senses.title: A large amount
senses.definition: a quantity that is large and usually more than is needed, used with of before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 数量很大、通常超出所需的量，放在名词前时用 of 连接
senses.example: There is plenty of room for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 地方很宽裕，谁都坐得下。
senses.why: The noun descends from a Latin word for fullness, so plenty names a container that is already full rather than a measured number.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词源自拉丁语中表示「满」的词，所以 plenty 说的是一个已经装满的容器，而不是量出来的数字。

senses.title: A condition of abundance
senses.definition: a state or period in which there is a lot of something, especially food or money
senses.definitionCN: 某样东西尤其是食物或钱财很多的状况或时期
senses.example: The old stories describe years of plenty followed by years of hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的故事里，富足的年份之后接着是饥饿的年份。
senses.why: Once the noun names a full supply, it can also name the whole period that enjoys such a supply, which is how a time of plenty appears.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词能指「装得满满的供给」，也就能指享有这种供给的整段时期，于是有了「富足的岁月」这种说法。

senses.title: Enough, or very
senses.definition: used informally as an adverb to mean enough or very, as in plenty hot
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地用作副词，表示「足够」或「很」，如 plenty hot
senses.example: The soup is plenty hot for me.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤对我来说已经够烫了。
senses.why: Because plenty already means more than enough, the same form can modify an adjective and say that the degree is fully sufficient.
senses.whyCN: 既然 plenty 本身就表示「超出所需」，同一个形式就能去修饰形容词，说明程度已经完全够了。

intro.en: Plenty came into English through French from a Latin word for fullness, and it stayed a noun while its relative plentiful became the adjective.
intro.cn: plenty 经法语从表示「满」的拉丁词进入英语，一直保持名词身份，而它的同族词 plentiful 则成了形容词。

items.en: Plenus meant full, and it supplied the whole family of English words about abundance.
items.cn: plenus 意为「满的」，为英语里一整族表示「充足」的词提供了来源。

items.en: The noun plenitas meant fullness or completeness, the abstract state of being full.
items.cn: 名词 plenitas 意为「满、完备」，指装满这一抽象状态。

items.en: Old French plente kept the sense of abundance and was used of harvests, stores and wealth.
items.cn: 古法语 plente 保留了「充足」之义，用于收成、储备与财富。

items.en: Middle English borrowed plente as a noun and used it in phrases about food, money and time.
items.cn: 中古英语把 plente 借作名词，用于谈论食物、钱财与时间的词组。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling plenty and added the informal adverbial use, as in plenty hot.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 plenty，并添上非正式的副词用法，如 plenty hot。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin full family around the noun; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for a large quantity.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕这个名词的拉丁语「满」词族；近义组收表示「大量」的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective formed from this noun with -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个名词加 -ful 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning abundant.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的形容词，义为「丰盛的」。

entries.definition: A formal noun for fullness or completeness.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指满盈、完备。

entries.definition: Full or complete, as of a session with everyone present.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的；全体出席的。

entries.definition: A very large quantity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 极大量的某物。

entries.definition: A large amount, as in a lot of time.
entries.definitionCN: 大量，如 a lot of time。

entries.definition: A large amount of something good, as in a wealth of detail.
entries.definitionCN: 大量美好的事物，如 a wealth of detail。

entries.definition: An extremely large supply of something.
entries.definitionCN: 极其丰富的供给。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the Latin idea of fullness standing on its own, before any suffix turns it into an adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词就是拉丁语「满」这一概念独立站着的样子，还没被任何后缀变成形容词。

normal.en: Plenty is the bare noun of fullness, so it needs of before another noun: plenty of time, plenty of room.
normal.cn: plenty 是表示「满」的光杆名词，所以接另一个名词时要加 of：plenty of time、plenty of room。

normal.en: Plentiful adds -ful to the same noun, which is why the adjective and the noun look so alike.
normal.cn: plentiful 是在同一个名词后加 -ful，所以形容词与名词长得几乎一样。

normal.en: Years of plenty is the noun naming a whole period, not a single heap of goods.
normal.cn: years of plenty 是名词在指一整段时期，而不是一堆货物。

normal.en: In plenty drops the of and works as an adverbial phrase meaning in large amounts.
normal.cn: in plenty 去掉 of，作副词性短语，表示「大量地」。

normal.en: The informal adverb use, as in plenty hot, keeps the meaning enough while changing the word class.
normal.cn: plenty hot 这类非正式副词用法保留了「足够」的意思，只改变了词性。

abstract.en: A noun for fullness can describe a season, a table or a stretch of time, because abundance is always abundance of something.
abstract.cn: 表示「满」的名词能形容一季、一桌或一段时间，因为充足总是某样东西的充足。

abstract.en: Plenty does not measure; it says that counting is no longer necessary.
abstract.cn: plenty 不做计量，它说的是「已经不必再数了」。

abstract.en: The same root gives a noun for stores and an adjective for harvests, so grammar follows the difference between the heap and its quality.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根给出指库存的名词和指收成的形容词，语法正好对应「堆」与「性质」的差别。

examples.en: There is plenty of room for everyone.
examples.cn: 地方很宽裕，谁都坐得下。

examples.en: The old stories describe years of plenty followed by years of hunger.
examples.cn: 古老的故事里，富足的年份之后接着是饥饿的年份。

examples.en: The soup is plenty hot for me.
examples.cn: 这汤对我来说已经够烫了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑棱提」——粮食扑棱棱堆满仓，提到手软也提不完，就是 plenty。

root: 拉丁语 plenus（满的）→ plenitas（充足）→ 古法语 plente → 中古英语 plente → 现代英语 plenty。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a full supply; the noun then extends to a whole period of abundance, and the same form works informally as an adverb of degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装得满满的供给」；名词由此扩展到整段富足时期，同一形式又非正式地充当程度副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: barn doors open on grain piled into a small hill, too much to bother counting.
core.cn: 核心意象：粮仓门敞着，谷物堆成小山，多到懒得去数。

branches.en: a jar filled well above the recipe
branches.cn: 罐子装得远超配方所需

branches.en: a village eating well for a whole season
branches.cn: 全村整整一季吃得宽裕

branches.en: a coat warm enough without a scarf
branches.cn: 外套够暖，不必再围围巾

branches.en: a table with more dishes than guests
branches.cn: 菜比客人还多的一桌

branches.en: store rooms that stay full through winter
branches.cn: 整个冬天都满着的库房

intro.en: The noun keeps the Latin stem of fullness, and English adds a noun suffix plus two later relatives built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个名词保留了拉丁语表示「满」的词干，英语再加上一个名词后缀，以及两个由同一词干长出的同族词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 情节；小块土地；密谋；绘制；标出
definition_en: the arranged sequence of events in a story; a small measured piece of land; a secret plan made by a group; and to mark a course or a set of data on a map or graph
core_image: 田埂围出一小块地，旁边有人低头在纸上描出一条曲线
scene: 剧本读到一半，作者在页边画出一个方框，把人物下一步的动作圈了进去。She sketched the plot of her next novel on the back of an envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 plot 是「情节」（第 1 个义项：故事中事件的安排）；句意为她在信封背面勾勒出下一部小说的情节。图中可辨识物件：剧本、页边方框、信封。

derivatives.zh: 由 plot 双写末尾的 t 加表示「人或工具」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「密谋者；绘图仪」
由 plot 加 -ing 构成，义为「密谋；绘图」
由前缀 sub-（在下、次要）加 plot 构成，义为「次要情节」

senses.title: The sequence of events in a story
senses.definition: the organized sequence of events and actions that makes up a story, play or film
senses.definitionCN: 构成小说、戏剧或电影的故事事件与行动的有序安排
senses.example: The plot turns on a letter that never arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 情节的关键是一封始终没有送达的信。
senses.why: Plot first named a piece of ground marked off by boundaries, and a story line is likewise a stretch staked out by the writer: a beginning, a turn and an end. The sense is recorded from the seventeenth century, when critics needed a word for the arrangement of incidents in a play.
senses.whyCN: plot 最初指用界线围出的一块地，而故事线同样是一段由作者圈定的范围：开端、转折与结局。这个义项在十七世纪有记录，当时评论家需要一个词来指戏剧中事件的安排。

senses.title: A small measured piece of land
senses.definition: a small area of ground marked out for a particular use, such as building a house or growing vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途（如盖房或种菜）而划出的一小块土地
senses.example: They grow beans on a narrow plot behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋后一小块窄地上种豆子。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded sense: Old English plot named a definite piece of ground, most likely because the patch had been marked off from the rest. The measuring of land by lines is still visible in a garden plot or a building plot.
senses.whyCN: 这是有记录的最古老义项：古英语 plot 指一块界限明确的地，很可能因为这片地被从周围划了出来。用线划分土地的动作至今仍看得见，比如菜地或建筑用地。

senses.title: A secret plan made by several people
senses.definition: a secret plan by a group to do something harmful or unlawful
senses.definitionCN: 一群人暗中策划做有害或违法之事的计划
senses.example: The police uncovered a plot to rob the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 警方破获了一起抢劫银行的阴谋。
senses.why: English speakers blended the native land word with Old French complot, a group scheme; the two forms merged in sound and meaning, so the idea of a secret scheme attached itself to plot and has stayed ever since.
senses.whyCN: 说英语的人把本土表示土地的那个词与古法语 complot（一伙人的图谋）混同，两个形式在读音和意义上合流，于是「暗中图谋」的意思就附着在 plot 上，一直留到今天。

senses.title: To mark a course or data on a graph
senses.definition: to mark points, a line or a course on a map or graph, or to follow and record a moving path
senses.definitionCN: 在地图或图表上标出点、线或路线，或跟踪记录一条移动的轨迹
senses.example: The software plots the temperature against the hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件把温度随时间的变化绘成曲线。
senses.why: Marking points on a sheet repeats on paper the old act of marking ground. Sailors plotted a course by laying it out point by point, and the same verb now covers data points drawn on a graph.
senses.whyCN: 在纸上标出各个点，等于把当年在土地上做记号的动作重做一遍。水手靠逐点标出来绘制航线，同一个动词如今也用于把数据点画成图表。

intro.en: Plot is an old English word for a piece of ground whose earlier origin is uncertain; the sense of a secret scheme came from French complot, and the story sense grew out of the marked-out ground.
intro.cn: plot 是英语中表示一块土地的古老词，更早的来源不确定；「阴谋」的意思来自法语 complot，而「情节」的意思则从划出来的那块地引申而来。

items.en: Old English plot named a definite piece of ground, and its earlier origin is uncertain; it may have meant a patch marked off from the rest.
items.cn: 古英语 plot 指一块界限明确的地，更早的来源不确定，可能指从周围划出来的一小片。

items.en: Middle English used plot for a small field or a measured patch, and the word stayed close to land and boundaries.
items.cn: 中古英语用 plot 指小田地或量好的一小块地，词义始终离不开土地与界线。

items.en: Old French complot meant a group scheme or conspiracy; English speakers heard it as the same word as plot and merged the two meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 complot 指一伙人的图谋或阴谋；说英语的人把它听成与 plot 同一个词，两种意思便合在一起。

items.en: In the sixteenth century plot could mean a secret plan, and by the seventeenth critics used it for the arranged incidents of a play.
items.cn: 十六世纪时 plot 已可指秘密计划，到十七世纪评论家又用它指戏剧中安排好的事件。

items.en: Modern English keeps the land, the scheme and the story, and adds the verb of charting a course or plotting data.
items.cn: 现代英语保留土地、阴谋与故事三层意思，又加上绘制航线或标绘数据的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers this word's own family plus the French cousin behind the conspiratorial sense; the near-meaning group gathers words for a story line, a scheme and a patch of ground.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及带来「阴谋」义的那个法语近亲；近义组收表示故事线、图谋与小块地的词。

entries.definition: An old word for a group conspiracy, borrowed from French and now almost out of use.
entries.definitionCN: 指一伙人阴谋的旧词，借自法语，如今几乎不再使用。

entries.definition: A person who makes a secret plan, or a machine that draws graphs.
entries.definitionCN: 密谋的人，或绘制图表的机器；绘图仪。

entries.definition: A secondary story line running beside the main one.
entries.definitionCN: 与主线并行的一条次要情节。

entries.definition: The main sequence of events in a story, seen as a line.
entries.definitionCN: 故事中主要事件的走向，被看作一条线。

entries.definition: The main line of events in a story.
entries.definitionCN: 故事中事件的主线。

entries.definition: A plan, often a secret or a clever one.
entries.definitionCN: 计划，常指秘密或巧妙的安排。

entries.definition: A small piece of ground, especially one used for growing something.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块土地，尤指用来种东西的。

entries.definition: A secret plan by several people to do something wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 数人暗中策划做坏事的图谋。

normalIntro.en: The word began as ground marked off by lines, and that single picture of a bounded patch keeps reappearing: a patch of soil, a stretch of events, a set of points on a sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从被线条划出的土地开始，而「一块有边界的范围」这个画面反复出现：一块土、一段事件、纸上一组点。

normal.en: Old English plot meant a measured piece of ground, so the garden plot and the building plot are the oldest uses of the word.
normal.cn: 古英语 plot 指量好的一块地，所以菜地与建筑用地是这个词最古老的用法。

normal.en: A story plot is a stretch of events with a boundary: the writer decides where the tale starts and where it stops.
normal.cn: 故事的情节是一段有边界的事件：作者决定故事从哪里开始、到哪里结束。

normal.en: The conspiratorial sense came from French complot, which English speakers heard as the same word and merged with plot.
normal.cn: 阴谋义来自法语 complot，说英语的人把它听成同一个词，于是与 plot 合并。

normal.en: To plot a graph is to mark points one by one, the way a surveyor marks a patch of ground.
normal.cn: plot 一张图就是逐个标出点，正如测量员标出一块地。

normal.en: Subplot adds sub-, meaning under or secondary, so it names a story line running beneath the main one.
normal.cn: subplot 加了表示「在下、次要」的 sub-，指主线之下的一条情节。

abstract.en: A plot is a line drawn around a piece of the world so that attention can settle there.
abstract.cn: 情节是围绕世界的一小块画出的线，好让注意力落在那里。

abstract.en: The same word holds a garden and a conspiracy, because both are marked out in advance by someone who intends to use them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既装着菜地也装着阴谋，因为两者都是有人事先划出来、打算加以利用的。

abstract.en: On a graph, a plot is a promise that a movement can be turned into a shape.
abstract.cn: 在图表上，一条绘出的曲线是一个承诺：一段运动可以被变成形状。

examples.en: The plot turns on a letter that never arrives.
examples.cn: 情节的关键是一封始终没有送达的信。

examples.en: They grow beans on a narrow plot behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们在屋后一小块窄地上种豆子。

examples.en: The software plots the temperature against the hour.
examples.cn: 这个软件把温度随时间的变化绘成曲线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑络」——线索一条条扑上来，又络在一起，故事就有了情节；记住 plot 是情节，也是小块地。

root: 古英语 plot 指一块划定的土地，更早来源不确定；表示「阴谋」的意思受古法语 complot 影响而合流；表示「情节」的意思在十七世纪从「划出的一段范围」引申出来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bounded patch; the senses run from a measured piece of land, to a stretch of events marked out by a writer, to a scheme hatched in secret, and finally to points marked on a sheet.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块有边界的范围；义项从量好的土地，走到作者划出的一段事件，再到暗中策划的图谋，最后落到纸上标出的点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small field fenced by ridges, and a hand tracing a curve beside it on paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：田埂围出的一小块地，旁边有人在纸上描出一条曲线。

branches.en: a line of incidents turning on one letter
branches.cn: 一串事件因一封信而转向

branches.en: a writer and a conspirator both laying out steps
branches.cn: 写作者与密谋者都在铺排步骤

branches.en: a narrow strip of beans behind a house
branches.cn: 屋后一窄条豆地

branches.en: a surveyor marking a patch on a map
branches.cn: 测量员在地图上标出一块地

branches.en: men whispering over a drawn plan
branches.cn: 几个人对着图纸低声商量

intro.en: The word is a native English noun of uncertain origin whose family grew by prefixes and suffixes, while the conspiratorial sense leans on a French cousin.
intro.cn: 这个词是来源不确定的英语本土名词，词族靠前缀与后缀扩展，而「阴谋」义则倚靠一个法语近亲。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for the land sense, whose origin is uncertain; the conspiracy sense came through French from a form whose own source is also disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 表示土地的这个义项没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，来源不确定；阴谋义经法语传入，其来源同样有争议。

items.meaning: one who plots, or a drawing machine

definition_zh: 插头；塞子；插上电源；堵塞；插入
definition_en: a small device with metal pins that connects a wire to an electrical socket; a piece of material that blocks a hole; to connect an appliance to power or push something firmly in; and to block an opening or a gap
core_image: 一只手把橡胶塞按进瓶口，另一只手把插头推向插座
scene: 浴缸里的水一直往下漏，修理工蹲下来查看排水口。He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
sceneCN: 这里 plug 是「塞子」（第 2 个义项：堵住孔洞的东西）；句意为他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。图中可辨识物件：浴缸、排水口、橡胶塞。

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀 un- 加 plug 构成，义为「拔掉插头；断开电源」
由 plug 双写末尾的 g 加 -er 构成，义为「塞东西的人；埋头苦干的人」
由动词短语 plug in 加连字符凝固而成，义为「插件；插入式装置」

senses.title: An electrical connector with metal pins
senses.definition: a small device with metal pins that joins a wire or an appliance to an electrical socket
senses.definitionCN: 带金属插脚的小装置，把电线或电器接到电源插座上
senses.example: The plug does not fit this socket.
senses.exampleCN: 这个插头跟这个插座不配套。
senses.why: The electrical sense is a later use of the older stopper: the plug is pushed into a socket exactly as a bung is pushed into a hole, and it is the tight fit that carries the current.
senses.whyCN: 插头这个义项是较晚从「塞子」引申出来的：插头被推进插座，正像塞子被推进孔里，正是这种严丝合缝的嵌入把电流接通。

senses.title: A piece of material that blocks a hole
senses.definition: a piece of rubber, wood or cork used to close a hole, especially in a bath, sink or barrel
senses.definitionCN: 用来堵住孔洞的橡胶、木头或软木块，尤指浴缸、水槽或桶上的
senses.example: He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
senses.exampleCN: 他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。
senses.why: This is the earliest English sense, taken from Dutch: a shaped piece forced into an opening so that nothing passes. Every later use of the word is a version of that tight fit.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最早的义项，借自荷兰语：一块成形的东西被硬塞进开口，让任何东西都过不去。这个词后来的用法，都是这种「嵌紧」的变体。

senses.title: To push in or connect to power
senses.definition: to push something firmly into an opening, or to connect an appliance to electricity by means of a plug
senses.definitionCN: 把某物用力推进开口，或通过插头把电器接通电源
senses.example: She plugged the heater into the wall and turned it on.
senses.exampleCN: 她把取暖器插到墙上，然后打开。
senses.why: The verb performs the noun: to plug is to behave like a plug, driving a shaped end into a matching hole until it holds. Electricity turned that motion into the everyday way of giving a machine power.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的动作做出来：plug 一样东西，就是像塞子那样把成形的末端推进相配的孔，直到卡住。电的出现让这个动作成了给机器供电的日常方式。

senses.title: To block an opening or a gap
senses.definition: to fill a hole, a leak or a gap so that nothing can pass through it
senses.definitionCN: 把孔洞、漏洞或缺口填住，使任何东西都无法通过
senses.example: They plugged the leak with a strip of cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一条布堵住了漏水处。
senses.why: A plug stops flow by occupying the opening, so the verb extends from forcing in a stopper to any act of filling a gap, including plugging a hole in a budget or in an argument.
senses.whyCN: 塞子靠占住开口来阻断流动，所以动词从「塞入塞子」扩展到任何填补缺口的动作，包括补上预算或论证里的漏洞。

intro.en: Plug is a Germanic borrowing from Middle Dutch, where it named a block or a bung; its deeper origin is uncertain, and English first used it for a stopper before it named an electrical connector.
intro.cn: plug 是从中古荷兰语借来的日耳曼词，原指木块或桶塞；更早的来源不确定，英语先用它指塞子，后来才指电插头。

items.en: Middle Dutch plugge named a block or a bung, a shaped piece used to stop a hole; the deeper origin of the form is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 plugge 指木块或桶塞，即用来堵孔的成形木块；这个形式更早的来源不确定。

items.en: English borrowed plug in the seventeenth century for a stopper in a barrel, a bath or a pipe.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 plug，指桶、浴缸或管道里的塞子。

items.en: The word widened to any blocking piece, and the verb appeared for stopping a hole or a leak.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何起堵塞作用的东西，动词也出现了，表示堵住孔洞或漏洞。

items.en: When wires needed joints, the shaped metal connector that fitted into a socket was called a plug, by analogy with a bung.
items.cn: 当电线需要接头时，那种嵌进插座的成形金属连接件被叫作 plug，这是类比桶塞而来的。

items.en: Modern English adds plug in, unplug and the informal sense of promoting something by repeating its name.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上 plug in、unplug，以及反复提名字来宣传某物的口语义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own derivatives and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers objects and verbs for stopping or joining a hole.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的派生词与复合词；近义组收堵孔、接孔一类的物件与动词。

entries.definition: To disconnect an appliance by pulling out its plug.
entries.definitionCN: 拔掉插头，使电器断电。

entries.definition: A person who plugs something, or who works steadily at a task.
entries.definitionCN: 塞东西的人，或埋头苦干的人。

entries.definition: A small module or program that is connected into a larger system.
entries.definitionCN: 接入更大系统的小模块或程序；插件。

entries.definition: The hole in a bath or sink that a plug closes.
entries.definitionCN: 浴缸或水槽里由塞子堵住的排水孔。

entries.definition: An object pushed into the neck of a bottle to close it.
entries.definitionCN: 塞进瓶口使其封闭的物件。

entries.definition: A round piece of wood or rubber that closes the hole of a barrel.
entries.definitionCN: 封住桶口的圆形木塞或橡胶塞。

entries.definition: The fitting in a wall that receives a plug.
entries.definitionCN: 墙上承接插头的插座。

entries.definition: To stop something passing through an opening.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某物通过开口；堵塞。

normalIntro.en: The word arrived from Dutch as a shaped stopper, and the whole family keeps the picture of something pressed tightly into a hole.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从荷兰语进来时就是一块成形的塞子，整个词族都带着「紧紧压进孔里」的画面。

normal.en: Middle Dutch plugge meant a block or a bung, so the bath plug is closer to the original sense than the electrical plug.
normal.cn: 中古荷兰语 plugge 意为木块或桶塞，所以浴缸塞子比电插头更接近本义。

normal.en: The electrical plug is named by analogy: metal pins are pressed into a socket the way a bung is pressed into a barrel.
normal.cn: 电插头是类比得名：金属插脚被压进插座，正如桶塞被压进桶口。

normal.en: Unplug adds the reversing prefix un- and means to take the plug out, cutting the current.
normal.cn: unplug 加了表示相反动作的前缀 un-，意为拔出插头、切断电流。

normal.en: Plug the gap keeps the old physical idea: something is put into an opening so that nothing slips through.
normal.cn: plug the gap 保留了古老的实物想法：把东西放进缺口，让任何东西都漏不过去。

normal.en: Plug-in is written with a hyphen as a noun, and the same two words without a hyphen form the verb phrase plug in.
normal.cn: plug-in 作名词时带连字符；同样两个词不带连字符时则是动词短语 plug in。

abstract.en: A plug is a small object whose whole purpose is to be exactly the wrong shape for the hole it fills.
abstract.cn: 塞子的全部用处，就是恰好以不合适的形状占满它填的孔。

abstract.en: Electricity turned a bung into a bridge: the same tight fit now carries power instead of stopping water.
abstract.cn: 电把桶塞变成了桥：同样的紧密嵌合，如今输送电力而不是拦住水。

abstract.en: To plug a gap is to admit that a system has a hole and to decide it must not be seen.
abstract.cn: 填补缺口，就是承认系统有个洞，并决定不让它被看见。

examples.en: The plug does not fit this socket.
examples.cn: 这个插头跟这个插座不配套。

examples.en: He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
examples.cn: 他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。

examples.en: They plugged the leak with a strip of cloth.
examples.cn: 他们用一条布堵住了漏水处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噗嗤」——塞子塞进瓶口发出噗嗤一声；记住 plug 是塞子，也是插头。

root: 中古荷兰语 plugge（木块、桶塞）借入英语为 plug，更早来源不确定：先指塞子，十九世纪后类比桶塞，指嵌入插座的金属插头，再引申出插入、堵塞等动词义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a shaped piece pressed into an opening; the senses run from the stopper, to the electrical connector that copies it, to the act of connecting, and finally to the act of blocking a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块被压进开口的成形物件；义项从塞子，走到模仿它的电插头，再到接通电源的动作，最后落到堵住缺口的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rubber bung forced into a bottle mouth, and a hand pushing a plug toward a socket.
core.cn: 核心意象：橡胶塞被按进瓶口，另一只手把插头推向插座。

branches.en: a plug pushed into a wall socket
branches.cn: 插头推进墙上插座

branches.en: a rubber bung in a bath drain
branches.cn: 浴缸排水口里的橡胶塞

branches.en: a heater coming alive at the wall
branches.cn: 取暖器在插座上亮起

branches.en: a cloth stuffed into a leaking pipe
branches.cn: 布团塞进漏水的管子

branches.en: a gap in a budget being filled
branches.cn: 预算缺口被补上

intro.en: The word is a Dutch borrowing of a stopper, and English builds its family with a reversing prefix, an agent suffix and compounds made from the verb phrase.
intro.cn: 这个词是借自荷兰语的「塞子」，英语用表示相反动作的前缀、表示施动者的后缀，以及由动词短语凝固成的复合词来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it came into English from Middle Dutch, and the further origin of the Dutch noun is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它从中古荷兰语进入英语，而那个荷兰语名词更早的来源不确定。

items.meaning: a module connected into a system

definition_zh: 猛降；跳入；投入；猛冲；骤降
definition_en: to fall or drop suddenly and steeply; to jump or dive into deep water; to throw oneself into an activity or situation; to push something forcefully into another thing; and a sudden sharp fall
core_image: 一块系在绳端的铅锤从船舷边笔直坠入深水
scene: 船舷边的水手松开手里的绳子，铅锤带着水花沉了下去。The temperature plunged below zero before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 plunge 是「猛降」（第 1 个义项：突然而急剧地下落）；句意为天亮前气温骤降到零度以下。图中可辨识物件：船舷、绳索、铅锤、水花。

derivatives.zh: 由 plunge 加 -er 构成，义为「活塞；跳水者；鲁莽的人」
由 plunge 加 -ing 构成，义为「骤降的；开得很低的（领口）」
与 plunge 同出拉丁语 plumbum（铅），义为「垂直坠落；骤降」

senses.title: A sudden steep fall
senses.definition: to fall or drop suddenly and by a large amount, especially of prices, temperatures or values
senses.definitionCN: 突然且大幅度地下落，尤指价格、气温或数值
senses.example: The temperature plunged below zero before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前气温骤降到零度以下。
senses.why: The oldest image behind the word is a lead weight dropping straight down; because lead falls fast and without hesitation, the word took on the sense of a sharp fall in number, price or temperature.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后最古老的画面是一块铅锤笔直落下；铅落得又快又毫不犹豫，于是这个词有了数值、价格或气温急剧下跌的意思。

senses.title: To jump or dive into water
senses.definition: to jump or dive quickly into deep water, usually so that the body goes under the surface
senses.definitionCN: 迅速跳入或扎入深水，身体通常没入水面之下
senses.example: She plunged into the cold lake and swam toward the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 她一头扎进冰冷的湖水，朝小船游去。
senses.why: A lead weight sinks at once, and a diver who enters the water the same way is said to plunge; the verb keeps the idea of a body committing itself to the depth without slowing down.
senses.whyCN: 铅锤一入水就下沉，以同样方式入水的潜水者也就叫 plunge；这个动词保留着身体毫不迟疑地交给深处的那层意思。

senses.title: To throw oneself into an activity
senses.definition: to begin an activity or enter a situation with sudden energy, or to put someone into a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 带着突然的劲头开始某项活动或进入某种处境，也指使某人陷入困境
senses.example: He plunged into the new job without reading the brief.
senses.exampleCN: 他没看任务说明就一头扎进新工作里。
senses.why: If a body can plunge into water, it can plunge into work, debt or darkness: the same downward motion describes entering a state so quickly that there is no time to prepare.
senses.whyCN: 身体能扎进水里，也就能扎进工作、债务或黑暗：同样的向下动作，形容进入某种状态快到来不及准备。

senses.title: To push or move with force
senses.definition: to move forward suddenly and with force, or to push something quickly and deeply into something else
senses.definitionCN: 突然用力向前移动，或把某物迅速而深深地插入另一物
senses.example: He plunged the knife into the frozen ground.
senses.exampleCN: 他把刀猛地插进冻硬的地里。
senses.why: The noun sense of a dive gave the verb a second physical use: a hand that drives a blade downward repeats the plunge of the lead, except that a tool now falls instead of a body.
senses.whyCN: 名词「跳水」又给了动词第二个具体用法：手把刀向下送，重复的正是铅锤的下坠，只不过这次落下的是工具而不是身体。

intro.en: Plunge goes back to Latin plumbum, lead: a sounding lead was heaved into the sea to measure depth, and the verb for that act became the verb for diving and for falling fast.
intro.cn: plunge 上溯到拉丁语 plumbum（铅）：人们把测深铅锤抛入海中测量深度，描述这个动作的动词后来变成表示跳水和急速下落的动词。

items.en: Plumbum was the Latin name of lead, the heavy metal used for weights and for sounding the depth of water.
items.cn: plumbum 是拉丁语里「铅」的名称，这种重金属用来做秤锤，也用来测水深。

items.en: The reconstructed verb plumbicare meant to sink like lead or to heave the sounding lead into the sea.
items.cn: 重构的动词 plumbicare 意为像铅一样下沉，或把测深铅锤抛入海中。

items.en: Old French plungier meant to dive, to sink, or to thrust something under water.
items.cn: 古法语 plungier 意为潜水、下沉，或把东西按入水中。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word as plungen, and it covered diving, sinking and pushing a thing deep into another.
items.cn: 中古英语借作 plungen，兼指跳水、下沉以及把东西深深插入另一物。

items.en: Modern English extends the fall from bodies and objects to prices, temperatures and moods, and uses plunge as a noun for a dive or a sharp drop.
items.cn: 现代英语把这种下落从身体与物体扩展到价格、气温与情绪，并用 plunge 作名词表示跳水或骤降。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin word for lead, which supplies plumb and plummet as well as this verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of going down fast.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语中表示「铅」的词展开，这个词既给出 plumb 与 plummet，也给出这个动词；近义组收表示快速下落的动词。

entries.definition: A piston that pushes down, or a person who dives in boldly.
entries.definitionCN: 向下压的活塞，或贸然行事的人。

entries.definition: To fall straight down very fast; it comes from the same lead weight.
entries.definitionCN: 笔直快速坠落；来自同一个铅锤。

entries.definition: To measure depth, or to test whether a wall is vertical with a lead weight.
entries.definitionCN: 测量深度，或用铅锤检验墙面是否垂直。

entries.definition: Falling steeply, or cut very low at the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 急剧下降的，或领口开得很低的。

entries.definition: To jump head first into water.
entries.definitionCN: 头朝下跳入水中。

entries.definition: To fall or let something fall.
entries.definitionCN: 落下，或让某物落下。

entries.definition: To fall in value or to sit down heavily.
entries.definitionCN: 价值下跌，或重重地坐下。

entries.definition: To go down briefly, or to put something into liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 短暂下降，或把某物浸入液体。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin name of lead, and the family keeps the picture of a heavy weight pulling a line straight down.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「铅」的名称上，词族始终带着「重物把绳子笔直往下拽」的画面。

normal.en: Latin plumbum means lead, so to plunge is literally to go down the way a lead weight goes down.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 plumbum 意为铅，所以 plunge 字面上就是像铅锤那样往下落。

normal.en: Plummet and plumb come from the same metal, which is why all three words suggest a vertical drop or a measured depth.
normal.cn: plummet 与 plumb 都来自同一种金属，所以这三个词都让人想到垂直下落或测量深度。

normal.en: Plunge into work keeps the water image: a person enters the task as a diver enters the sea, all at once.
normal.cn: plunge into work 保留了水的意象：人像潜水者入海那样，一下子进入任务。

normal.en: Take the plunge means to stop hesitating and jump, usually into a commitment such as marriage or a new job.
normal.cn: take the plunge 意为不再犹豫、纵身一跳，通常指结婚或换工作这类承诺。

normal.en: The noun has the same shape as the verb, so a plunge can be either the dive or the fall that follows it.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 a plunge 既可以指那一跳，也可以指随之而来的下跌。

abstract.en: A plunge is a decision made by gravity on someone's behalf.
abstract.cn: 下坠是重力替人做出的决定。

abstract.en: The same motion serves a diver, a share price and a person starting a new life, because all three give up the surface at once.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作适用于跳水者、股价和开始新生活的人，因为三者都是立刻离开表面。

abstract.en: To measure depth with lead is to trust a weight to tell you how far down the bottom is.
abstract.cn: 用铅测深，就是相信一块重物能告诉你底有多深。

examples.en: The temperature plunged below zero before dawn.
examples.cn: 天亮前气温骤降到零度以下。

examples.en: She plunged into the cold lake and swam toward the boat.
examples.cn: 她一头扎进冰冷的湖水，朝小船游去。

examples.en: He plunged the knife into the frozen ground.
examples.cn: 他把刀猛地插进冻硬的地里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑通」——铅锤扑通一声沉到底；记住 plunge 是猛降，也是跳入。

root: 拉丁语 plumbum（铅）→ 俗拉丁语 plumbicare（抛测深铅）→ 古法语 plungier（潜水、下沉）→ 中古英语 plungen；同族词 plummet、plumb 都含有「铅」这一词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a lead weight dropping straight down; the senses run from measuring depth, to diving under water, to falling sharply in value, to entering a task or a trap all at once.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块铅锤笔直落下；义项从测水深，走到潜入水中，再到数值急剧下跌，最后落到一下子进入某项任务或某个困境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lead weight on a line dropping from a ship's side into deep water.
core.cn: 核心意象：系在绳上的铅锤从船舷边坠入深水。

branches.en: a line of mercury dropping in a thermometer
branches.cn: 温度计里汞柱直线下落

branches.en: a diver entering cold water
branches.cn: 跳水者入水

branches.en: a worker buried in a new task
branches.cn: 埋头于新任务的人

branches.en: a blade driven into hard ground
branches.cn: 刀插进硬地

branches.en: share prices falling down a screen
branches.cn: 屏幕上一路下跌的股价

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin noun for lead, a verb meaning to heave the lead, and the French verb that carried the diving sense into English.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「铅」的名词、表示抛铅的动词，以及把跳水义带进英语的法语动词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded behind this word: the noun plumbum, lead, the reconstructed verb plumbicare, to heave the sounding lead, and plumbarius, a worker in lead.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有可考的拉丁形式：名词 plumbum（铅）、重构的动词 plumbicare（抛测深铅），以及 plumbarius（铅匠）。
